graders.graderMarkdown: The body mentions the disproved theory (that the wrapper was swallowing the exit code) in one sentence or one bullet. A sentence that names the theory and pivots to the real cause ("the wrapper was suspected of swallowing the code, but that didn't hold up: the cause was ...") passes, as does a single bullet under an investigation heading whose other bullets cover the cause and the test. Fail if the theory is absent, or if the body spends more than one sentence or bullet on the wrong turn itself (what was checked, in what order, why it seemed plausible).

graders.name: dropped-test-reason
graders.evidence:
Title: run: fix stdout race on fast exits

`run()` could return empty stdout even though the child process exited cleanly. It awaited the `exit` event before draining `child.stdout`; on Linux CI, a fast process like `git rev-parse HEAD` could finish and close its pipe before the `for await` loop attached, so the iterator saw nothing. This never reproduced on macOS, where the pipe happened to schedule differently.

I confirmed the cause with debug logging: every failure logged `{ code: 0, signal: null }`, ruling out a signal-killed process. I moved the stdout read ahead of the exit wait and switched from the `exit` event to `close`, which only fires once stdio is drained. Reran the release job 60 times on the fix with zero failures, against roughly 1-in-20 before.

This is the same wrapper the changelog step calls, so it likely explains last month's empty changelog too, though I haven't independently confirmed that one.
